purpose.en: Bodytomy is a whole-body anatomy viewer — rotate the figure, tap a part to select it, and use the region picker and probe line to see the muscles, bones and vessels beneath it.
purpose.ko: Bodytomy는 전신 해부학 뷰어입니다 — 인체 모형을 회전시키고, 부위를 탭해서 선택하고, 영역 선택기와 탐침선을 사용해 그 아래의 근육, 뼈, 혈관을 확인하세요.
purpose.zh: Bodytomy 是一款全身解剖查看器——旋转人体模型，点按部位进行选择，使用区域选择器和探针线查看其下方的肌肉、骨骼和血管。
purpose.hi: Bodytomy एक पूर्ण-शरीर एनाटॉमी व्यूअर है — आकृति को घुमाएं, किसी भाग को टैप करके चुनें, और उसके नीचे की मांसपेशियों, हड्डियों व रक्तवाहिकाओं को देखने के लिए क्षेत्र चयनकर्ता और प्रोब लाइन का उपयोग करें।
purpose.es: Bodytomy es un visor de anatomía de cuerpo completo: gira la figura, toca una parte para seleccionarla y usa el selector de región y la línea de sonda para ver los músculos, huesos y vasos debajo de ella.
purpose.fr: Bodytomy est un visualiseur d'anatomie du corps entier — faites pivoter la silhouette, touchez une partie pour la sélectionner, puis utilisez le sélecteur de région et la ligne de sonde pour voir les muscles, os et vaisseaux en dessous.
purpose.ar: Bodytomy عارض تشريح لكامل الجسم — أدر النموذج، اضغط على أي جزء لتحديده، واستخدم أداة اختيار المنطقة وخط المسبار لرؤية العضلات والعظام والأوعية الدموية تحته.
purpose.pt: O Bodytomy é um visualizador de anatomia de corpo inteiro — gire a figura, toque em uma parte para selecioná-la e use o seletor de região e a linha de sonda para ver os músculos, ossos e vasos abaixo dela.
purpose.ru: Bodytomy — это просмотрщик анатомии всего тела: вращайте фигуру, нажимайте на часть, чтобы выбрать её, и используйте селектор области и линию зонда, чтобы увидеть мышцы, кости и сосуды под ней.
purpose.de: Bodytomy ist ein Ganzkörper-Anatomie-Viewer — drehe die Figur, tippe auf einen Teil, um ihn auszuwählen, und nutze die Regionsauswahl und die Sondenlinie, um die darunterliegenden Muskeln, Knochen und Gefäße zu sehen.
purpose.ja: Bodytomyは全身解剖ビューアです — 人体モデルを回転させ、部位をタップして選択し、領域セレクターとプローブラインを使って、その下の筋肉・骨・血管を確認できます。
purpose.tr: Bodytomy tüm vücut anatomi görüntüleyicisidir — figürü döndürün, bir parçaya dokunarak seçin ve altındaki kasları, kemikleri ve damarları görmek için bölge seçiciyi ve prob çizgisini kullanın.
purpose.vi: Bodytomy là trình xem giải phẫu toàn thân — xoay mô hình, chạm vào một bộ phận để chọn, và dùng bộ chọn vùng cùng đường dò để xem cơ, xương và mạch máu bên dưới.
purpose.it: Bodytomy è un visualizzatore di anatomia a corpo intero: ruota la figura, tocca una parte per selezionarla e usa il selettore di regione e la linea sonda per vedere muscoli, ossa e vasi sottostanti.
purpose.fa: Bodytomy یک نمایشگر آناتومی تمام‌بدن است — پیکر را بچرخانید، روی بخشی ضربه بزنید تا انتخاب شود، و از انتخاب‌گر ناحیه و خط کاوش برای دیدن عضلات، استخوان‌ها و رگ‌های زیر آن استفاده کنید.
purpose.pl: Bodytomy to przeglądarka anatomii całego ciała — obracaj postać, dotknij części, aby ją wybrać, i użyj selektora regionu oraz linii sondy, aby zobaczyć mięśnie, kości i naczynia pod spodem.
purpose.uk: Bodytomy — це переглядач анатомії всього тіла: обертайте фігуру, торкніться частини, щоб вибрати її, і використовуйте селектор ділянки та лінію зонда, щоб побачити м'язи, кістки й судини під нею.
purpose.nl: Bodytomy is een anatomie-viewer voor het hele lichaam — draai de figuur, tik op een onderdeel om het te selecteren en gebruik de regioselector en probelijn om de spieren, botten en vaten eronder te zien.
purpose.sv: Bodytomy är en anatomivisare för hela kroppen — rotera figuren, tryck på en del för att välja den och använd regionväljaren och sondlinjen för att se muskler, ben och kärl under den.
purpose.cs: Bodytomy je prohlížeč anatomie celého těla — otáčejte postavou, klepnutím na část ji vyberte a pomocí výběru oblasti a sondovací linky zobrazte svaly, kosti a cévy pod ní.
purpose.el: Το Bodytomy είναι ένα πρόγραμμα προβολής ανατομίας ολόκληρου σώματος — περιστρέψτε τη φιγούρα, πατήστε ένα μέρος για να το επιλέξετε και χρησιμοποιήστε τον επιλογέα περιοχής και τη γραμμή ανίχνευσης για να δείτε τους μύες, τα οστά και τα αγγεία από κάτω.

model.title: Whole body
model.subtitle: Muscles, bones & vessels · whole body (real anatomy)

parts.name: Gluteus maximus
parts.info: The body’s biggest muscle. Extends the hip — powers you up stairs, out of chairs, and into a sprint.
parts.from: Back of the pelvis and sacrum
parts.to: Upper femur and the IT band

parts.name: Gluteus medius
parts.info: Steadies your pelvis every time you stand on one leg — the key muscle behind a level, wobble-free stride.

parts.name: Tensor fasciae latae
parts.info: A small hip flexor that tensions the IT band running down the outer thigh, helping steady the knee.

parts.name: Iliopsoas
parts.info: Your deepest hip flexor — lifts the thigh for every step, and pulls you up from lying flat.

parts.name: Rectus femoris
parts.info: The middle quad. The only quad that also flexes the hip — straightens the knee and drives a kick.

parts.name: Vastus lateralis
parts.info: The outer quad, and the largest — a straight-ahead knee extender behind squats, jumps, and cycling.

parts.name: Vastus medialis
parts.info: The teardrop-shaped inner quad. Extends the knee and keeps the kneecap tracking straight.

parts.name: Sartorius
parts.info: The longest muscle in the body — a thin strap that helps you sit cross-legged (hip up + out, knee bent).

parts.name: Adductor longus
parts.info: Pulls the thigh inward — squeezing a ball between the knees, or stabilizing during side-steps.

parts.name: Adductor magnus
parts.info: The big, deep inner-thigh muscle — part adductor, part hamstring-helper on hip extension.
parts.to: Inner femur, down to the knee

parts.name: Gracilis
parts.info: A slender strap down the inner thigh — assists adduction and knee bending.

parts.name: Biceps femoris — long head
parts.info: The hamstring head that crosses BOTH the hip and the knee: it extends the hip as well as bending the knee, which is why it is the one that brakes your leg at the end of a sprint stride.

parts.name: Biceps femoris — short head
parts.info: The deeper, shorter head. It starts on the thigh bone itself, so it crosses the knee ONLY — it bends and outwardly rotates the knee and has no action at the hip at all.

parts.name: Semitendinosus
parts.info: The middle hamstring — half muscle, half long tendon. Bends the knee, extends the hip.

parts.name: Semimembranosus
parts.info: The deepest hamstring, with its belly low near the knee. Bends the knee, extends the hip.

parts.name: Tibialis anterior
parts.info: Front of the shin. Lifts your foot so your toes clear the ground — shin splints live here.

parts.name: Fibularis longus
parts.info: Runs down the outer calf and hooks behind the ankle — everts the foot and guards against rolled ankles.

parts.name: Gastrocnemius — medial head
parts.info: The inner and larger of the calf's two heads. It makes the inner bulge of the calf, points the foot down, and helps bend the knee.
parts.from: Back of the inner femoral condyle

parts.name: Gastrocnemius — lateral head
parts.info: The outer and smaller of the calf's two heads. Same job as the inner head — pointing the foot and helping bend the knee — from the outer side of the knee.
parts.from: Back of the outer femoral condyle

parts.name: Soleus
parts.info: The flat endurance muscle under the calf — working every second you simply stand.
parts.from: Back of the tibia and fibula

parts.name: Clavicle (collarbone)
parts.info: The strut that holds the shoulder out away from the chest.

parts.name: Scapula (shoulder blade)
parts.info: A flat triangular bone that glides over the ribs — the shoulder's moving base.
parts.from: Floats on the back of the ribcage

parts.name: Humerus (upper arm bone)
parts.info: The single long bone between shoulder and elbow.

parts.name: Radius
parts.info: The forearm bone on the thumb side; it rotates to turn the palm over.

parts.name: Ulna
parts.info: The forearm bone on the little-finger side; it forms the point of the elbow.

parts.name: Hand bones
parts.info: Wrist, palm and fingers, shown as one simple shape.

parts.name: Skull
parts.info: The bony case around the brain; shown as a simple shape, with no facial detail.

parts.name: Cervical spine
parts.info: The seven neck vertebrae that let the head turn and nod.

parts.name: Thoracic spine
parts.info: The twelve vertebrae the ribs attach to; it curves gently backwards.

parts.name: Lumbar spine
parts.info: The five lowest vertebrae — the part of the spine that carries the most load when you lift.

parts.name: Sternum (breastbone)
parts.info: The flat bone down the front of the chest that the ribs join.

parts.name: Ribcage & costal cartilage
parts.info: The curved bones that shield the heart and lungs and move with every breath.

parts.name: Rectus abdominis
parts.info: Curls you forward — the muscle you feel in a sit-up.

parts.name: External oblique
parts.info: Twists and side-bends the trunk, and helps hold the waist in.

parts.name: Latissimus dorsi
parts.info: Pulls the arm down and back — the muscle that does a pull-up.
parts.to: Front of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Trapezius — upper (descending) part
parts.info: The part you shrug with. It runs down from the skull and neck to the collarbone and lifts the shoulder blade.
parts.from: Base of the skull and the cervical spine

parts.name: Trapezius — middle (transverse) part
parts.info: The horizontal middle band. It pulls the shoulder blades together — the squeeze in a row.
parts.to: Acromion and spine of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Trapezius — lower (ascending) part
parts.info: The lower band. It pulls the shoulder blade DOWN and helps rotate it upward when you reach overhead.
parts.to: Ridge on the back of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Pectoralis major — upper (clavicular) part
parts.info: The upper chest fibres, running from the collarbone. They raise the arm FORWARD and upward — the part an incline press loads.

parts.name: Pectoralis major — middle (sternocostal) part
parts.info: The big middle sheet from the breastbone and ribs. It is the bulk of the chest and the main mover in a press-up or a flat press.

parts.name: Pectoralis major — lower (abdominal) part
parts.info: The small lower slip from the abdominal sheath. It pulls the arm down and in, the way a dip or a straight-arm pulldown does.
parts.from: Sheath of the rectus abdominis, over the lower ribs

parts.name: Pectoralis minor
parts.info: Sits under the big chest muscle and tips the shoulder blade forward.

parts.name: Serratus anterior
parts.info: Wraps the ribs and holds the shoulder blade flat against them when you reach forward.
parts.to: Inner edge of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Deltoid — front (clavicular) part
parts.info: The front third of the shoulder cap. Lifts the arm FORWARD and turns it inward.
parts.to: Middle of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Deltoid — middle (acromial) part
parts.info: The middle third — the one that lifts the arm straight out to the side. It is the main abductor of the shoulder.
parts.to: Middle of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Deltoid — rear (spinal) part
parts.info: The back third. Pulls the arm BACKWARD and turns it outward — the half of the shoulder most people under-train.
parts.from: Ridge on the back of the shoulder blade
parts.to: Middle of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Supraspinatus
parts.info: Part of the rotator cuff — starts the arm moving away from the body.
parts.to: Head of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Infraspinatus
parts.info: Part of the rotator cuff — turns the arm outward and steadies the joint.
parts.to: Head of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Biceps brachii — long head
parts.info: The outer head. Its tendon runs through the shoulder joint itself and over the top of the arm bone, so it helps steady the shoulder as well as bending the elbow.

parts.name: Biceps brachii — short head
parts.info: The inner head. It starts on the beak-shaped process at the front of the shoulder blade and helps lift the arm forward as well as bending the elbow.
parts.from: Coracoid process of the shoulder blade

parts.name: Triceps brachii — long head
parts.info: The only triceps head that crosses the shoulder as well as the elbow: it straightens the elbow AND pulls the arm back and in toward the body.
parts.from: Shoulder blade, just below the socket

parts.name: Triceps brachii — lateral head
parts.info: The outer head, and the one that gives the back of the arm its horseshoe shape. Straightens the elbow only.
parts.from: Back of the upper arm bone, above the groove

parts.name: Triceps brachii — medial head
parts.info: The deep head, hidden under the other two. It works at every elbow angle and does most of the light, everyday straightening.
parts.from: Back of the upper arm bone, below the groove

parts.name: Brachialis
parts.info: Lies under the biceps and does most of the work of bending the elbow.
parts.from: Front of the upper arm bone

parts.name: Brachioradialis
parts.info: The ridge of muscle on the thumb side of the forearm; helps bend the elbow.

parts.name: Sternocleidomastoid
parts.info: The cord you see down the side of the neck; turns the head to the opposite side.

parts.name: Aorta
parts.info: The body's largest artery — every heartbeat pushes blood down it toward the legs.
parts.to: Splits into the two iliac arteries

parts.name: Inferior vena cava
parts.info: The big vein that returns blood from everything below the chest back to the heart.

parts.name: Common carotid artery
parts.info: Carries blood up the neck to the brain — the pulse you can feel beside the windpipe.

parts.name: Internal jugular vein
parts.info: Drains blood from the brain back down the neck.

parts.name: Inguinal ligament
parts.info: Bridges the front of the pelvis, forming the floor of the inguinal canal.

parts.name: Achilles tendon
parts.info: The body's strongest tendon — transmits calf-muscle force to the heel with every step.

parts.name: Iliotibial (IT) band
parts.info: A thick fascial band running down the outside of the thigh, stabilizing the hip and knee.

parts.name: Gluteus minimus
parts.info: Deepest of the three glutes. Abducts the hip and, with gluteus medius, keeps the pelvis level when you stand on one leg.

parts.name: Piriformis
parts.info: Deep rotator running from the sacrum out to the hip. Rotates the thigh outward; the sciatic nerve passes right beside it.

parts.name: Obturator internus
parts.info: Deep hip rotator that turns a sharp corner inside the pelvis to reach the femur. Rotates the thigh outward.
parts.from: Inner rim of the obturator foramen
parts.to: Medial side of the greater trochanter

parts.name: Obturator externus
parts.info: Sits on the outer face of the obturator membrane. Rotates the thigh outward and helps steady the hip joint.
parts.from: Outer rim of the obturator foramen

parts.name: Quadratus femoris
parts.info: Short, square deep rotator below the other rotators. Strong external rotation of the thigh.

parts.name: Gemellus superior
parts.info: One of the twin muscles flanking obturator internus. Assists external rotation of the hip.

parts.name: Gemellus inferior
parts.info: The lower twin beside obturator internus, from a slightly lower origin on the ischial tuberosity. Also assists external rotation of the hip.

parts.name: Vastus intermedius
parts.info: The quadriceps head hidden underneath rectus femoris, wrapped straight around the femur shaft. Extends the knee.
parts.from: Front and side of the femur shaft

parts.name: Adductor brevis
parts.info: Short inner-thigh muscle behind adductor longus. Pulls the thigh toward the midline.
parts.from: Body and inferior ramus of the pubis
parts.to: Upper linea aspera of the femur

parts.name: Adductor minimus
parts.info: The uppermost slip of adductor magnus, often described separately. Adducts and externally rotates the thigh.
parts.to: Upper linea aspera of the femur

parts.name: Pectineus
parts.info: Flat muscle bridging the pubis to the femur at the top of the inner thigh. Flexes and adducts the hip.

parts.name: Popliteus
parts.info: Small muscle behind the knee that "unlocks" a fully straightened knee so it can bend again.

parts.name: Plantaris
parts.info: Tiny belly with a very long thin tendon running down the calf. Weakly assists calf plantarflexion; absent in some people.
parts.from: Lateral supracondylar line of the femur

parts.name: Tibialis posterior
parts.info: Deepest calf muscle. Inverts the foot and holds up the arch during stance.
parts.from: Back of the tibia, fibula and interosseous membrane

parts.name: Fibularis brevis
parts.info: Runs behind the lateral ankle bone. Everts the foot and helps point the toes.

parts.name: Fibularis tertius
parts.info: Small front-of-leg muscle sharing a tendon sheath with the toe extensors. Lifts and everts the foot.

parts.name: Extensor hallucis longus
parts.info: Lifts the big toe and helps pull the foot upward when you swing your leg through.
parts.to: Base of the big toe’s distal phalanx

parts.name: Extensor digitorum longus
parts.info: Straightens the four lesser toes and lifts the foot so the toes clear the ground when walking.
parts.from: Upper front of the fibula and lateral tibia
parts.to: Middle and distal phalanges of toes 2–5

parts.name: Flexor hallucis longus
parts.info: Curls the big toe and gives the final push-off at the end of each step.
parts.to: Base of the big toe’s distal phalanx

parts.name: Flexor digitorum longus
parts.info: Curls the four lesser toes and helps grip the ground during push-off.

parts.name: Quadratus lumborum
parts.info: Deep square muscle from the pelvis to the last rib. Side-bends the trunk and hikes the hip.
parts.to: Twelfth rib and upper lumbar vertebrae

parts.name: Transversus abdominis
parts.info: Deepest abdominal layer, wrapping the waist like a belt. Compresses the abdomen and braces the spine.
parts.from: Lower ribs, thoracolumbar fascia and iliac crest

parts.name: Internal oblique
parts.info: Middle abdominal wall layer, fibres running upward and inward. Rotates the trunk to the same side and compresses the belly.

parts.name: Diaphragm
parts.info: The dome-shaped main breathing muscle sealing the bottom of the chest. Flattens on inhale to pull air in.
parts.from: Lower ribs, sternum and lumbar spine

parts.name: Transversus thoracis
parts.info: Thin fan on the inner surface of the front chest wall. Draws the costal cartilages down during forced exhalation.

parts.name: Iliocostalis
parts.info: The most lateral column of the erector spinae. Extends and side-bends the spine.
parts.from: Sacrum, iliac crest and lower ribs
parts.to: Angles of the ribs and cervical transverse processes

parts.name: Longissimus
parts.info: The long middle column of the erector spinae, running the length of the back. Extends the spine and steadies it upright.
parts.to: Ribs, thoracic and cervical transverse processes, mastoid process

parts.name: Spinalis
parts.info: The innermost erector spinae column, hugging the spinous processes. Extends the spine.
parts.from: Upper lumbar and lower thoracic spinous processes
parts.to: Upper thoracic and cervical spinous processes

parts.name: Semispinalis
parts.info: Deep layer spanning several vertebrae at a time up into the skull. Extends and rotates the spine and head.
parts.to: Spinous processes above and the occipital bone

parts.name: Multifidus
parts.info: Short deep bundles bridging two to four vertebrae. The spine’s fine-grained segmental stabiliser.
parts.to: Spinous processes two to four levels above

parts.name: Rhomboid major
parts.info: Sheet between the spine and the shoulder blade. Pulls the shoulder blade back and toward the spine.

parts.name: Rhomboid minor
parts.info: The smaller rhomboid just above rhomboid major. Retracts and slightly elevates the shoulder blade.
parts.to: Medial border of the scapula at the spine of the scapula

parts.name: Levator scapulae
parts.info: Strap from the neck to the top corner of the shoulder blade. Shrugs and downwardly rotates the scapula.

parts.name: Serratus posterior superior
parts.info: Thin sheet under the rhomboids. Lifts the upper ribs during inhalation.

parts.name: Serratus posterior inferior
parts.info: Thin sheet at the base of the ribcage. Draws the lower ribs down and back during forced exhalation.

parts.name: Teres major
parts.info: Thick strap from the lower shoulder blade to the humerus, working with latissimus dorsi. Adducts and internally rotates the arm.
parts.to: Medial lip of the bicipital groove

parts.name: Teres minor
parts.info: Rotator-cuff muscle below infraspinatus. Rotates the arm outward and holds the humeral head in its socket.

parts.name: Subscapularis
parts.info: The rotator cuff muscle on the front of the shoulder blade. Rotates the arm inward and stabilises the shoulder.

parts.name: Coracobrachialis
parts.info: Slim muscle deep in the armpit beside the short head of biceps. Flexes and adducts the arm at the shoulder.

parts.name: Anconeus
parts.info: Small triangular muscle at the back of the elbow. Assists triceps in straightening the elbow.

parts.name: Pronator teres
parts.info: The top muscle of the flexor group, crossing the forearm diagonally. Turns the palm downward and helps bend the elbow.
parts.from: Medial epicondyle of the humerus and coronoid process of the ulna

parts.name: Flexor carpi radialis
parts.info: Bends the wrist and pulls it toward the thumb side. Its tendon is the one you can feel at the front of the wrist.
parts.to: Base of the second and third metacarpals

parts.name: Palmaris longus
parts.info: Slender wrist flexor that tenses the palm’s fascia. Missing in roughly one person in seven.

parts.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
parts.info: Bends the wrist and pulls it toward the little-finger side. The most medial of the superficial flexors.
parts.from: Medial epicondyle of the humerus and the olecranon

parts.name: Flexor digitorum superficialis
parts.info: Bends the middle knuckles of the four fingers — the layer just under the surface flexors.
parts.from: Medial epicondyle, ulna and upper radius

parts.name: Flexor digitorum profundus
parts.info: The only muscle that bends the fingertips. Sits deepest in the front of the forearm.
parts.from: Front and medial surface of the ulna

parts.name: Flexor pollicis longus
parts.info: Bends the tip of the thumb — the only muscle that does.
parts.from: Front of the radius and interosseous membrane

parts.name: Pronator quadratus
parts.info: Square muscle just above the wrist joining the two forearm bones. The prime mover for turning the palm down.

parts.name: Extensor carpi radialis longus
parts.info: Extends the wrist and pulls it toward the thumb side. Runs just behind brachioradialis.
parts.from: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus

parts.name: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
parts.info: The shorter wrist extensor beside its longus partner — commonly the sore one in tennis elbow.

parts.name: Extensor digitorum
parts.info: Straightens the four fingers. Its tendons are the ridges you see on the back of your hand.

parts.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris
parts.info: Extends the wrist and pulls it toward the little-finger side.
parts.from: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus and the ulna

parts.name: Extensor digiti minimi
parts.info: A dedicated extensor for the little finger, letting it straighten independently.
parts.to: Extensor hood of the little finger

parts.name: Supinator
parts.info: Wraps around the upper radius. Turns the palm upward — the opposite of the pronators.

parts.name: Abductor pollicis longus
parts.info: Pulls the thumb away from the palm. Forms the front edge of the anatomical snuffbox.
parts.from: Back of the ulna, radius and interosseous membrane

parts.name: Extensor pollicis brevis
parts.info: Straightens the base joint of the thumb. Shares a tendon compartment with abductor pollicis longus.
parts.from: Back of the radius and interosseous membrane

parts.name: Extensor pollicis longus
parts.info: Straightens the tip of the thumb and hooks around a bony ridge on the radius on its way there.
parts.from: Back of the ulna and interosseous membrane

parts.name: Extensor indicis
parts.info: Lets the index finger point independently of the others.
parts.from: Back of the ulna and interosseous membrane
parts.to: Extensor hood of the index finger

parts.name: Temporalis
parts.info: Broad fan on the side of the skull that passes under the cheekbone. Closes the jaw — you can feel it move at your temple.

parts.name: Masseter
parts.info: The thick chewing muscle at the angle of the jaw, pound for pound one of the strongest in the body.
parts.to: Angle and ramus of the mandible

parts.name: Platysma
parts.info: A wide sheet of muscle just under the skin of the neck. Tenses the neck skin and pulls the corners of the mouth down.
parts.from: Fascia over the upper chest and shoulder
parts.to: Lower border of the mandible and skin of the lower face

parts.name: Sternohyoid
parts.info: Strap muscle at the front of the throat. Pulls the hyoid bone down after swallowing.
parts.from: Back of the manubrium and medial clavicle

parts.name: Omohyoid
parts.info: Two-bellied strap crossing the neck diagonally from the shoulder blade. Depresses the hyoid bone.

parts.name: Digastric
parts.info: Two bellies joined by a tendon looped under the jaw. Opens the mouth and lifts the hyoid when swallowing.
parts.from: Mastoid notch of the temporal bone and the digastric fossa of the mandible
parts.to: Body of the hyoid bone via the intermediate tendon

parts.name: Mandible (jawbone)
parts.info: The lower jaw — the only freely movable bone in the skull, hinged at the temporomandibular joint.

parts.name: Common iliac artery
parts.info: One of the two branches the aorta splits into at the lower abdomen, carrying blood toward the pelvis and leg.

parts.name: External iliac artery
parts.info: Runs down along the pelvic brim and becomes the femoral artery as it passes under the inguinal ligament into the thigh.

parts.name: Internal iliac artery
parts.info: Turns down into the pelvis to supply the pelvic organs, the buttock and the hip.

parts.name: Common iliac vein
parts.info: Joins its partner from the other side to form the inferior vena cava, returning blood from the pelvis and leg.

parts.name: External iliac vein
parts.info: The continuation of the femoral vein above the inguinal ligament, carrying leg blood back into the pelvis.

parts.name: Internal iliac vein
parts.info: Drains the pelvic organs, buttock and hip into the common iliac vein.

parts.name: Subclavian artery
parts.info: Passes under the collarbone and becomes the axillary and then the brachial artery — the main supply to the arm.

parts.name: Subclavian vein
parts.info: The main venous return from the arm, joining the internal jugular behind the collarbone.

parts.name: Brachiocephalic vein
parts.info: Formed where the subclavian and internal jugular veins meet; the two sides join to make the superior vena cava.

parts.name: Brachiocephalic trunk
parts.info: The first and largest branch off the aortic arch, splitting into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.

parts.name: Superior vena cava
parts.info: The great vein returning blood from the head, neck and arms into the right atrium of the heart.

parts.name: Renal artery
parts.info: Short, wide branch straight off the aorta to the kidney — the kidneys take about a fifth of the heart’s output.

parts.name: Renal vein
parts.info: Carries filtered blood from the kidney back into the inferior vena cava.

parts.name: Celiac trunk
parts.info: A short trunk off the aorta that immediately splits three ways to the stomach, liver and spleen.

parts.name: Superior mesenteric artery
parts.info: Supplies the small intestine and the first part of the colon.

parts.name: Inferior mesenteric artery
parts.info: Supplies the last part of the colon and the upper rectum.

parts.name: Pulmonary artery
parts.info: The one artery that carries oxygen-poor blood: from the right ventricle out to the lungs.

parts.name: Pulmonary vein
parts.info: The one vein that carries oxygen-rich blood: from the lungs back into the left atrium.

parts.name: Long plantar ligament
parts.info: Strong band along the sole from the heel forward. A main static support of the foot’s long arch.

parts.name: Flexor retinaculum of the wrist
parts.info: The band roofing the carpal tunnel. Holds the finger flexor tendons down — and is what is released in carpal tunnel surgery.

parts.name: Interosseous membrane (forearm)
parts.info: A fibrous sheet slung between the radius and ulna. Ties the two bones together and gives muscles extra attachment area.

parts.name: Interosseous membrane (leg)
parts.info: The fibrous sheet between the tibia and fibula, transferring load between them and anchoring the deep leg muscles.

parts.name: Epicranial aponeurosis
parts.info: The tough sheet across the top of the skull linking the forehead and back-of-head muscles of the scalp.

parts.name: Femoral artery (schematic path)
parts.info: Carries oxygenated blood down the thigh toward the leg. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Femoral vein (schematic path)
parts.info: Carries deoxygenated blood from the leg back toward the heart, alongside the femoral artery. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Great saphenous vein (schematic path)
parts.info: The body's longest vein — a superficial drainage route running just under the skin. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Anterior tibial artery (schematic path)
parts.info: Passes through the gap between shin bones to supply the front of the leg and foot. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Posterior tibial artery (schematic path)
parts.info: Runs down the back of the leg to supply the calf and sole of the foot. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Brachial artery (schematic path)
parts.info: Runs down the inner arm — the artery a blood-pressure cuff squeezes. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Basilic vein (schematic path)
parts.info: A superficial vein up the inner arm; often where blood is drawn. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Cephalic vein (schematic path)
parts.info: A superficial vein up the thumb side of the arm to the shoulder. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Patellar ligament (schematic path)
parts.info: Continues the quadriceps tendon below the kneecap, transmitting its pull to the shin. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Medial collateral ligament (MCL) (schematic path)
parts.info: Stabilizes the inner side of the knee against sideways force. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) (schematic path)
parts.info: Stabilizes the outer side of the knee against sideways force. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Plantar fascia (schematic path)
parts.info: A tough band along the sole, supporting the foot's arch. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Crural fascia band (schematic path)
parts.info: The sleeve of deep fascia wrapping the lower-leg muscles. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Thoracolumbar fascia (schematic path)
parts.info: A broad diamond of fascia across the low back that ties the trunk to the hips. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.

parts.name: Abdominal fascia (schematic path)
parts.info: The sheet that wraps the abdominal muscles and meets its partner down the midline. Drawn as a simplified schematic path: this structure is not present in the BodyParts3D source data, so its course is approximate.
